sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment of the tweet: the author's own attitude, or, for news-style headlines, the clear valence of the reported event. Choose neutral when the tone is mild, mixed, joking or purely informational.

criteria.positive: Clear enthusiasm, praise, love, gratitude, well-wishing, condolences/prayers, or eager anticipation ('can't wait', 'so excited', 'love', 'best', 'Happy...', '!!', <3, :-)). Also headlines reporting a clearly good event: a win, title, record, achievement, celebration, or someone 'delighted'. A plain announcement or plan is not positive unless it carries explicit excitement or praise.
criteria.neutral: Factual or routine news, schedules, event announcements, promotions, sign-ups, giveaways, ticket offers, questions, polls, rumors, requests to celebrities, and plans stated without strong feeling. Also play-by-play sports commentary, trivia, musings, and light banter or self-deprecating grumbles softened by humor ('lol', 'lmao', 'I'm dead', 'not ready for...'). Use it for minor mishaps and for mixed or ambiguous tone.
criteria.negative: Genuine disappointment, sadness, anger, annoyance, missing out on something wanted, loneliness, or pointed criticism, mockery, sarcasm or hostility toward people, teams, companies or politics. This includes argumentative replies rebutting someone. Cues: 'sucks', 'disappointed', 'can't go', 'miss', ':(', 'despise', '#sarcasm'. Also headlines reporting clearly bad events: attacks, deaths, funerals, arrests, deficits, scandals, failures, defects.
